Gate-activation hypothesis

The gate activates on verbs indicating personal certainty, belief, or knowledge (e.g., "know," "believe," "think," "certain"). It fires strongly when the subject is first-person ("I") or when the verb introduces a clause expressing a firm conviction, opinion, or realization about a situation, relationship, or fact.

Describes when the gate fires. It does not establish the transform’s causal output effect.
